task.description: Re-diagnose the async:false/shared-mode cross-connection-visibility regression TEST-RUNNER found at Step 5 (step-05-test-runner.json, FAIL, 18-19 reproducible failures). Determine scope (structural class vs. a handful of exceptions), rule in/out an Ecto Sandbox-native remedy, and hand CODE-DESIGNER a corrected mechanism for design §10. Diagnosis only -- no fix implementation.
acceptance_criteria: State whether the gap is structural (any async:false caller of provisioned_tenant!/1) or a bounded exception set, with a real count
Confirm or refute, with source evidence, whether Ecto's Sandbox library offers any mode that lets an async:false caller's connection see a commit made through a second Ecto.Repo's separate pool

Determine whether async:false callers were ever exposed to the ORIGINAL ISS-0113/ISS-0480 hazard (global mode-flip check-in) in the same way async:true callers were, or whether they need a structurally different remedy
Route to CODE-DESIGNER for a design rework of section 10, not implement anything

result.summary:
STRUCTURAL CLASS, CONFIRMED BY COUNT: 44 of 47 files calling `Letflow.TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!/1` (46 real callers per the design doc's own re-count, plus the ISS-0480 regression test itself = 47 grep hits including 2 prose-only false positives already excluded by the design's own §0 audit) are `async: false`. Verified directly this session: `grep -rl "provisioned_tenant!(" test --include=*.exs | grep -v tenant_fixture.ex` (47 hits) then reading each file's own `use Letflow.DataCase, async: ...` line individually (not grepping the bare string, which the design doc's §0 already documented as producing false positives from moduledoc prose). Only 2 real files are `async: true` today: secrets_test.exs and webhooks_test.exs (the ISS-0423/ISS-0113 §9 tranche) -- both ALREADY exercise the correct, working case (cross-connection commit visible via a fresh :auto-mode checkout, no problem there). Every one of the other 44, including test/letflow/tenant_provisioning/backfill_test.exs (TEST-RUNNER's fully root-caused example), is `async: false`. This is not a short list of exceptions like design §10.8's 2-file addendum -- it is the overwhelming majority shape of this call population, and every single one of them shares the identical mechanism (DataCase.setup/1's `{:shared, self()}` mode plus a same-process later read via Letflow.Repo). CODE-DESIGNER must treat 'any async:false caller of provisioned_tenant!/1 that later reads the provisioned data via its own Letflow.Repo connection' as the default case to design for, not a corner case.

ROOT CAUSE, confirmed by reading source directly (not inherited from TEST-RUNNER's report, though it independently arrives at the identical mechanism -- HANDOFF_PROTOCOL 1.1 checked):

1. `test/support/data_case.ex:15-23` -- for EVERY test (async or not), `setup/1` does `Sandbox.checkout(Letflow.Repo)`, which opens one real Postgres transaction on one connection, owned by the test process. For `async: false` only, it additionally calls `Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, {:shared, self()})` (line 19) -- this does NOT open a second transaction or a second connection; per `deps/ecto_sql/lib/ecto/adapters/sql/sandbox.ex:492-497` (quoted exactly: "after checking out a connection in manual mode, you can change the mode to {:shared, pid} ... this makes it so ALL PROCESSES CAN USE THE SAME CONNECTION as the one owned by the current process"), `{:shared, self()}` is purely an ownership-broadening declaration over the ONE connection/transaction already checked out in step 1 -- it lets OTHER processes (e.g. a Plug-pipeline process handling an HTTP request the test issues) reach that SAME transaction without an explicit `allow/3` call each time. It changes who may use the connection, never which connection or transaction is in play, and it never touches any other Ecto.Repo's pool.

2. Pre-ISS-0480, `provisioned_tenant!/1`'s first line was an unconditional `Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto)` -- run on THIS SAME connection/pool the caller's test process already owns. Per sandbox.ex:498-501 ("whenever you change the mode to :manual or :auto, all existing connections are checked in") and `DBConnection.Ownership.Manager`'s actual state machine (design doc lines 636-647, quoted from `deps/db_connection/lib/db_connection/ownership/manager.ex`), this call: (a) discarded the caller's own just-opened transaction from step 1 (empty at that point -- nothing lost, confirmed by the design's own §9.3 trace), (b) left the pool mode at `:auto` for the rest of the run (nothing ever restores `:manual`/`:shared`), and (c) crucially, the caller's OWN very next Repo call (the Tenant insert, still executing in the SAME test process, still targeting `Letflow.Repo`) auto-checked-out a FRESH connection under `:auto` mode and was recorded as that connection's owner -- so every subsequent query from that SAME test process (the provisioning writes, and the test body's own later reads) reused that SAME fresh connection. The caller never lost visibility into its own fixture's writes, because caller and fixture were, before ISS-0480, always the SAME process talking to the SAME repo's pool, just switching from a sandboxed/shared connection to an ambient :auto one partway through.

3. Post-ISS-0480 (this branch), `provisioned_tenant!/1` no longer touches `Letflow.Repo`'s mode at all. It redirects to `Letflow.Test.ProvisioningRepo` -- a WHOLLY SEPARATE `Ecto.Repo`, separate pool, separate `DBConnection.Ownership.Manager` process, separate physical Postgres backend connection -- via `Repo.put_dynamic_repo/1` (tenant_fixture.ex:291-301), does the Tenant insert and provisioning THERE under ProvisioningRepo's own `:auto` mode, then restores the dynamic-repo binding back to `Letflow.Repo` in an `after` block. This is exactly what design §10.2 intends and what makes RowApprovalTest-shaped victims (zero TenantFixture involvement) safe -- ProvisioningRepo's mode call structurally cannot reach Letflow.Repo's ownership manager. But it also means the write is now committed on a genuinely DIFFERENT connection than the one the caller's test process is using -- for an `async: false` caller, that connection is still the ORIGINAL one from data_case.ex's step 1, still inside its own open sandbox transaction/{:shared, self()} snapshot the whole time, because nothing in the new code path ever touches Letflow.Repo's mode or checkout state for that process anymore. Postgres transaction isolation means a separate connection's separate, already-committed transaction is invisible to a transaction that began earlier and is still open -- this is ordinary MVCC snapshot behavior, not a sandbox bug. Backfill.run/1's `Repo.all(Registration)` (lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning/backfill.ex:20), still running on the caller's original Letflow.Repo connection, sees 0 rows for a tenant genuinely committed via ProvisioningRepo a moment earlier. Reproduced byte-for-byte per TEST-RUNNER's step-05 report (`assert updated >= 1` fails with `left: 0`).

4. For `async: true` callers (secrets_test.exs/webhooks_test.exs), this is a non-issue -- confirmed by re-reading the design's own §9.4/§10.0: an async test's OWN Letflow.Repo connection is checked out (data_case.ex line 16) but NEVER put into `{:shared, ...}` mode, and the test itself never issues its own Sandbox.mode/2 call either. Its own subsequent Letflow.Repo queries (post-fixture) are ordinary `:auto`-adjacent Letflow.Repo pool queries -- Letflow.Repo's pool mode is left completely alone by the post-ISS-0480 fixture, so whatever the ambient project-wide state of Letflow.Repo's mode is (per the design's own §9.1/§9.4, :auto once any TenantFixture caller anywhere has run once), an async:true caller's later Letflow.Repo read auto-checks-out (or reuses) an ordinary connection under that SAME ambient :auto mode and sees the ProvisioningRepo-committed row exactly the same way any two ordinary :auto-mode Postgres clients see each other's commits -- real, unconditional, cross-connection COMMIT visibility, no sandbox transaction wrapping it at all. This is the intended, correct, and already-verified-working case (design moduledoc's `async: true` callers section, `test/letflow/iss0480_provisioning_repo_isolation_test.exs`).

ANSWER TO 'does Ecto Sandbox offer a mode that helps': NO, checked directly against `deps/ecto_sql/lib/ecto/adapters/sql/sandbox.ex`'s own moduledoc and `mode/2`/`checkout/2`/`allow/3` specs (lines 480-620ish). `{:shared, pid}` and `allow/3` both operate WITHIN one repo's one already-checked-out connection -- they broaden WHO may use it, never WHICH connection is in play, and neither has any mechanism to span two different `Ecto.Repo` modules' pools. There is no Sandbox API that makes one repo's checked-out connection see another repo's separate connection's commits; that would contradict the entire point of Sandbox (one transaction per test, rolled back at teardown) and would also be meaningless for `Letflow.Repo` vs `ProvisioningRepo` specifically since they are configured (design §10.2.2) as two distinct pools against the SAME physical database -- 'sharing a connection' across repo modules is not an Ecto/DBConnection concept that exists at any level; a connection belongs to exactly one pool.

ANSWER TO 'were async:false callers ever exposed to the original ISS-0113/ISS-0480 hazard the same way': NO -- this is the key asymmetry CODE-DESIGNER's rework needs to exploit, not paper over. The original hazard (a provisioning call's Sandbox.mode(:auto) globally checking in OTHER unrelated tests' connections) is a hazard that fires on WHOEVER's connection happens to be checked out from Letflow.Repo's pool AT THE MOMENT the mode call runs, regardless of the caller's own async declaration -- RowApprovalTest (async:true, zero TenantFixture involvement) was a victim precisely because :shared mode's exclusivity does NOT apply to it; :shared mode is only ever set for async:false tests (data_case.ex:18, `unless tags[:async]`), so under a plain `mix test` run, :shared mode is held by AT MOST ONE async:false test at any instant (ExUnit runs async:false tests strictly serially, one at a time, confirmed by the design's own §5.1 citation of ExUnit's documented scheduling) -- meaning an async:false caller's own connection, while it holds :shared mode, is NEVER the connection some OTHER concurrently-running test could accidentally check in via a stray :auto call, because no other test is running concurrently with it at all. The async:false population was never the vector for the cross-test blast-radius hazard ISS-0480 exists to close (that hazard is specifically about *concurrent* async tests colliding) -- it has its OWN, textually adjacent but mechanically distinct problem: a single test's own later read of its OWN fixture's own write, blocked by ordinary transaction-isolation once the write moved to a different connection. Fixing one does not fix or worsen the other; they were conflated only by both routing through the same `provisioned_tenant!/1` entry point.

WHAT THIS IMPLIES FOR THE REDESIGN (stated as constraints, not a specification -- CODE-DESIGNER's task, not mine): (a) async:true callers already have the correct fix and must not regress -- any redesign must leave the ProvisioningRepo-via-dynamic-repo path fully in effect for them. (b) async:false/shared-mode callers structurally need the provisioning WRITE to land on the SAME connection/transaction their own test process is already using (data_case.ex's step-1 checkout), not a different one -- the two candidate directions are (i) branch `provisioned_tenant!/1` on whether the CALLER's own test is async:false/shared-mode (detectable via `Sandbox.checkout/1`'s own returned mode, or via ExUnit `tags`/`Process` state passed through opts) and, for that branch ONLY, do the provisioning writes directly on `Letflow.Repo` under its already-established `{:shared, self()}` connection exactly as pre-ISS-0480 code did, since 9.3/9.4 above shows async:false was never the vector for the ORIGINAL hazard either -- OR (ii) some mechanism that makes ProvisioningRepo's commit visible to the caller's open transaction, which per the Sandbox source above does not exist and would require a schema-level workaround (e.g. `dblink`/`postgres_fdw`, or LISTEN/NOTIFY plus an explicit re-query, or Ecto's `Sandbox.allow/3`-style ownership handoff -- none of which apply across repos) -- so (i) is the direction with actual Sandbox-API support; (ii) should be treated as very likely a dead end unless CODE-DESIGNER finds a mechanism this diagnosis missed. Whichever direction is chosen, the design must restate and re-verify design doc's own §9.4/§10.0 safety argument for why branching does not reopen the ORIGINAL global-checkin hazard for async:true/RowApprovalTest-shaped victims -- in particular, direction (i) reintroduces a `Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, ...)`-adjacent call INSIDE `provisioned_tenant!/1` for the async:false branch only, and that call's own effect on Letflow.Repo's pool-wide mode (or lack thereof, if it can be scoped to `Sandbox.checkout`/no mode-change at all, since the caller already holds :shared mode and the fixture could simply issue its writes without calling Sandbox.mode/2 again) needs the same rigor §9.1-9.4 gave the current mechanism, not an assumption that 'it only affects async:false, so it's fine' -- exactly the class of unverified assumption this Step 5 failure itself came from.

SCOPE OF THE EXISTING REGRESSION TEST GAP (for TEST-DESIGNER once a fix ships): `test/letflow/iss0480_provisioning_repo_isolation_test.exs` only exercises the async:true/zero-involvement victim case (design's own admission, step-05's issue #1). It needs an ADDED case for an async:false/shared-mode caller's own read-after-provision visibility -- backfill_test.exs's existing 'ISS-0343 backfill' test already IS a real, currently-red instance of this; TEST-DESIGNER should not need to invent a new scenario, only confirm it goes red pre-fix and green post-fix per WF-03's fail-then-pass rule, and add at least one more of the 17-not-individually-root-caused failures (OnboardingTest or ContextTest, both simple HTTP-round-trip-through-Letflow.Repo shapes) as a second, independently-verified instance of the class rather than resting the whole regression proof on one file.
result.next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGNER for a rework of lib/letflow/design/iss0113-tenant-fixture-sandbox-restore-opt-in.md section 10 (new subsection, e.g. 10.9, additive per this design doc's own established convention of not silently deleting superseded content). The rework must: (1) keep the ProvisioningRepo/dynamic-repo mechanism fully in effect for async:true callers (already correct, already verified working); (2) add a distinct code path for async:false/shared-mode callers that makes the provisioning write land on the SAME connection/transaction the caller's own test process already holds via data_case.ex's {:shared, self()} setup, rather than on ProvisioningRepo's separate connection; (3) re-derive, with the same rigor as the existing design's 9.1-9.4/10.0, why the async:false branch cannot reopen the original ISS-0113/ISS-0480 global-checkin hazard -- this diagnosis found no exposure for async:false callers to that hazard (see reasoning above: :shared mode is held by at most one async:false test at a time, so it is never the accidental victim of a concurrent :auto flip), but CODE-DESIGNER must verify this claim independently rather than inherit it, per HANDOFF_PROTOCOL 1.1; (4) confirm no Sandbox/DBConnection API bridges two separate Ecto.Repo pools' connections (checked and refuted in this diagnosis against deps/ecto_sql/lib/ecto/adapters/sql/sandbox.ex directly -- CODE-DESIGNER should spot-check this claim too before building on it, same rule); (5) route the corrected design through CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR, then ELIXIR-DEV, SECURITY-REVIEWER/REVIEWER, TEST-DESIGNER (extend test/letflow/iss0480_provisioning_repo_isolation_test.exs per the gap noted above), TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR, and back to TEST-RUNNER for a full-suite re-run (scripts/test_parallel.sh, not only the two-file scoped run that missed this the first time). Do NOT merge feature/WF03-ISS0480-20260905 until a full-suite TEST-RUNNER PASS is obtained. ISS-0480 stays status: open.
